input.brief: Build a product page for small-batch pottery studio Kiln & Field. Their Oat Glaze Bowl is $46 and ships in 5 days. The maker throws and glazes it in Milwaukee. Give it a warm, tactile feel, and let a shopper put one bowl in the bag and see confirmation. There are no product photographs. Represent the bowl with an original drawing.

I need a site for a local bike repair shop. Second Spin does 48-hour tune-ups for $85. We are at 41 Elm Street and take bookings Tuesday to Saturday. Make booking easy to find and let a visitor pick a day to see the booking summary.

Make a page for Low Signal, a nonprofit community radio station. The live show is Field Notes with Ana Reyes, weekdays 7–9 am. Make Listen live the primary action. In this demo, toggle the control and show that the listener is live without loading audio. Make the station feel independent and specific.

Create the Salt Marsh Film Weekend landing page. June 13–14, Old Ferry Hall. The films are The Eel Road at 18:30 Friday and Birds at First Light at 16:00 Saturday. The visitor should be able to pick a screening and see its place, date and time. Use the program as the visual hook.

Give the City of Red Bluff an inviting page for its oral-history archive. Feature one interview with June Ortega, a sign painter interviewed in 1987, and one with Leon Wu, a bridge electrician interviewed in 1996. Opens a short excerpt for the selected interview. Use only those facts and short clearly labeled sample excerpts.

I need a site for a home insulation rebate. County residents can get up to $600 for crawlspace insulation. The application deadline is November 30. Show the three requirements: resident, primary home and licensed installer. Include a quick eligibility check that reports the result from those three answers.

Make a cold-chain monitoring board for the shipping lead. Truck 14 is at 9°C, limit 5°C. Truck 8 is at 3°C, Truck 11 at 4°C. The lead needs to find the excursion fast and switch between all trucks and excursions with two stateful filter buttons.

Make this feel premium. A theatre stage manager needs to find the rehearsal room that's running late. Studio B is six minutes late and Hall A is ready. Give them a way to view delayed rooms and restore the full list. Preserve those facts.

Create the morning greenhouse board. Bay 1 is 82% humidity and needs venting. Bay 2 is 65%, Bay 3 is 67%. Display 75% as the threshold. Let a grower acknowledge the alert and make the acknowledged state clear while retaining the reading.

Our support supervisor needs a queue summary. The East queue has 14 open and 3 past SLA, Central 6 open and 0 past SLA, West 11 open and 2 past SLA. Allow sorting by number past SLA. Make the sort direction and the active column easy to tell.

Show a building caretaker yesterday's electricity use: Boiler 120 kWh, Lighting 66 kWh, Lift 21 kWh. The caretaker can switch to today with Boiler 103, Lighting 58, Lift 16. Make the relative differences easy to read at a glance. Preserve units and show the active day.

A library manager needs today's hold pickup table: downtown 18 waiting, 4 expire today; north 11 waiting, 2 expire today; river 7 waiting, none expire today. Let them switch to branches that have holds expiring today and back, and communicate the count.

Build a reservation form for a ceramics workshop. The only times are Saturday at 10 am and Sunday at 2 pm. Collect a name, email and seat count from 1 to 4. Make mistakes clear and show a local confirmation with the chosen workshop details.

A tenant needs to report a broken common-area light. Collect building, location and a description, and offer Routine and Safety issue as urgency options. Make it usable by keyboard and show that the request was prepared locally after valid submission.

Build a return-label request for a record store. Ask for order number, email and one reason: damaged, wrong item, or changed mind. Show the selected reason in the confirmation. Missing or invalid entries need helpful messages and the page should keep what the customer entered.

Our community garden is registering volunteers for two shifts, Wednesday 5 pm or Saturday 9 am. Collect first name and shift, and allow an optional note about tools. Make it look like something a neighbor would want to use, with a confirmation that repeats the shift.

Create a museum group-visit request. Collect contact name, email, group size (1–25), and the choice Quiet visit or Guided visit. Show a clear confirmation with the group size and visit type. The form should work on a phone and never send the input away.

Build a quote request for an independent bookbinder. Ask for format (paperback, hardcover), number of copies (1–100) and contact email. Show the request summary after validating it. Use concrete copy and let the customer edit the entered details.

Make a phone screen for a passenger at a busy station. Train 487 to Milwaukee leaves at 17:42 from platform 6. A ticket is hidden behind one button. Revealing it shows ticket number T487-MK02 and a text fallback. Do not create a real scannable credential.

A trail crew checking a repair on a phone needs: Cliff Loop, east footbridge, deck boards loose. Let the crew mark it inspected and undo. The location and current state have to be readable outside in bright light.

Give a parent a quick phone view of a recital. Strings group checks in at Room 2 at 16:40, performs on Main Stage at 17:10. Let them switch between check-in and performance and make the selected view and location unambiguous.

A pickup basketball group needs to know if their court is open. Show Court 3, open until 21:30, and Court 5, closed for resurfacing. Give them an Open courts filter and a way to restore both. Avoid a decoration-heavy sports aesthetic.

Show a resident their food pantry collection time, Friday 11:15 at 18 Pine Avenue. Offer a Details button that reveals the instruction to bring a bag and check in at the side door. Make the address, date and time easy to find on a small phone.

Build a gallery visitor screen for the room they are standing in. Room 4 displays River Wall, 1972, by Maya Chen. A button shows or hides the material note, which reads Pigment on plaster. The art label should look considered and remain easy to scan.

Build notification settings for a community coworking space. Booking reminders start on, event announcements start off. Let the member change both and save. Show an accurate saved confirmation and keep the choices after reloading this page.

Design reading preferences for a cooking app. Offer Standard or Large text and Comfortable or Compact line spacing. Show the setting changes in the sample text 'Rest dough for 20 minutes.' Make it easy to reset to Standard and Comfortable.

Create a teammate role settings panel for Northline Books. Sam Lee is an Editor and Ari Bell is a Viewer. The operator can change Ari between Viewer and Editor, save the change, and see the resulting role. Use no live account or external calls.

Make study focus settings. The current session is 25 minutes with a 5-minute break. Choices are 25/5 or 50/10. Show which schedule is active, let me apply the other one, and reflect the new interval in a simple preview.

I need a supplier digest preferences screen. Frequency can be Daily, Weekly or Off. Initially it is Weekly, on Monday. Choosing Daily should hide the day choice, choosing Weekly should show it, and saving should summarize the choice clearly.

Build account display settings for a visitor center. Visitors can switch the example 2026-11-21 between 'November 21, 2026' and '21 November 2026'. They can choose Celsius or Fahrenheit and see 20°C or 68°F. Include a visible reset to the initial US date and Fahrenheit.

Build a saved trails screen for a hiking app that starts empty. Suggest one nearby route named Cedar Bend, 2.4 miles. Let the visitor save it from the empty state and see it in their list, then remove it to return to the initial state.

An independent publisher has no article drafts. Let an editor create a local named draft from the empty screen. Show the new draft and let them clear this demo item. Keep the language plain and make the transition to the first draft visible.

Build an empty search result for a public tool library. The query 'chain saw' has zero matches. Offer a related term 'pruning saw', which shows one available tool labeled Folding Pruning Saw. Make the reason for the empty result and the recovery action obvious.

An incoming bakery shift opens the handoff log and finds no notes. Show a direct way to add a first note, and let the person enter and save one locally so it replaces the empty state. Make it quick to use on a phone beside a prep station.

Create the empty exhibit shortlist for a museum trip. Suggest two exhibits, Light Studies and Objects in Transit. Let a teacher add either to the shortlist and see it there. Avoid illustrations that take up room without helping the planning task.

Show the empty upcoming-shifts view for a food-bank volunteer. Offer one available shift, Wednesday 4–6 pm, Packing. Let the volunteer reserve it locally and show the booked state in the same view. Make the result visible without another page.

direction.title: Performance program
direction.summary: Help a visitor compare scheduled performances. Put the program and the selected performance's time and practical details in one composition.

layout.skeleton: Pair a synopsis of the work with a program of selectable performances. Give each choice the same comparable facts and place the selected outcome beside the program.
layout.focus: An original close view of the decisive difference between the works, with a short plain-language description and a prominent selected performance.
layout.desktop: Use a strong title and a compact program next to the evidence from the selected work. Keep controls in reading order and the selected timetable close to its choice.
layout.mobile: Use a small featured scene and two readable choices near the result. Check that comparing the supplied cost and schedule works at 390 px and with enlarged text.
layout.rhythm: Group each performance's essential facts by aligned edges and shared rules. Give the selected work its own space instead of making every cover equally loud.

imagery.subject: Use original art or cleared assets to show the difference a visitor can use to choose. Keep a lightweight depiction immediately available, with a close detail when the decisive feature is small.
imagery.crop: Keep the decisive detail visible at desktop and phone widths. Retain any important timing or description as text.
imagery.fallback: Use a short factual description or labeled still when live art is unavailable. Keep all choices and journey information usable.

motion.trigger: Selecting a performance or an optional named detail
motion.effect: Update the chosen work and its details together. Animate the one visual change that communicates a difference.
motion.reduced: Show the final state immediately with the same labels and outcomes.

action.instruction: Give each choice a clear, persistent selected state. Keep the supplied facts needed for a decision visible and use each estimate's actual origin. When the brief gives enough facts, recalculate timing when a show or travel assumption changes.
action.label: Use the supplied performance name

direction.why: Understand what makes a show worth choosing and see whether it fits the practical constraints in the same visit.

sources.observation: The tested wireframe view displayed the original on a full canvas with labeled controls separate from it. Keep the decisive evidence available while more elaborate art loads.
The review uses a direct call to action and fast access to the first useful result. Keep the program immediately operable while visitors compare shows.

direction.credit: Original program direction from the Counterweight study with independently observed FunTech and YC references.

interaction.focus: Use a two-tone focus ring (2 px paper with 2 px ink outside) on the primary control.
interaction.accent_role: Use the accent as a focal fill under accent_foreground. Check contrast before using it as text.
interaction.keyboard: Expose the primary control by keyboard and announce pending and completed states.

assumptions: Use only the project facts and assets in the brief.
sample_candidate.handoff: Apply the composition to the actual content. Preserve the task and brand constraints. Fill label slots only with facts supplied by the brief. Use the source as design evidence. Omit support regions that would only repeat facts. Keep visual and document order aligned. Load the named fonts. Test the action, reading order and legibility at 390 px.

direction.title: Object hero: the product is the page
direction.summary: One featured product presented as a specimen, with the details and buy control in a single purchase block.

layout.skeleton: 7/5 split; the product image sits left, offset 1 column, and overlaps into a facts band
layout.focus: the featured product and one supplied detail that helps a buyer choose it, such as a tasting note, material, or finish
layout.desktop: Put the product name at the image edge. Give the deciding detail its own line. Keep the remaining facts and the add control together on the same column edges.
layout.mobile: At 390 px, use a shallow product crop up to 35% of the visible height. Keep the product name, deciding detail, size, price, supplied purchase facts, and add control together in reading order. Put the action in flow so it cannot cover a fact.
layout.rhythm: 96px between bands; the ledger uses a 24px baseline

imagery.subject: the product on a plain surface. If it has a label, make the product name and supplied variant or size the strongest lettering.
imagery.crop: tight, with the product cut by the right edge
imagery.fallback: Use the product name and its deciding detail as specimen typography when product imagery is unavailable.

motion.effect: bag count ticks and the pill settles 4px

action.instruction: One primary action attached to the product. Fill it from the brief's product, size and price, and never repeat it in a hero band
action.label: Add [product], [size] — [price]

direction.why: A first-time buyer needs one choice, not a catalogue. Making the object the hero and stating the brief's exact facts reads warm and exact.

sources.observation: Agrumea Farm hero: the product jars are the hero on cream paper with an oxblood shape and type set on a curve; the only CTA is a small pill on the featured jar ('Scopri il prodotto').

direction.credit: Agrumea Farm site (Awwwards submission; designer not verified)

interaction.focus: Use a two-tone focus ring (2 px paper with 2 px ink outside) on the primary control.
interaction.accent_role: Use the accent as a focal fill under accent_foreground. Check contrast before using it as text.
interaction.keyboard: Expose the primary control by keyboard and announce pending and completed states.

assumptions: Use only the project facts and assets in the brief.
selected.handoff: Apply the composition to the actual content. Preserve the task and brand constraints. Fill label slots only with facts supplied by the brief. Use the source as design evidence. Omit support regions that would only repeat facts. Keep visual and document order aligned. Load the named fonts. Test the action, reading order and legibility at 390 px.

calibration.reason: A legible, familiar intake supports the task, but misplaced focus after invalid input materially weakens recovery. The score is based only on the supplied description.

primary_action.input: Tab to One minute slower and press Enter; Shift+Tab to Call/Response and press Enter.
primary_action.expected: Show whether Hinge retains the buffer, then show the alternate fare and arrival.
primary_action.observed: Hinge costs £60 for two and initially arrives at 20:30 for the 20:40 train, exactly meeting the assumed 10-minute buffer. Its joined palms and mirrored lean communicate shared weight. The 15-minute walk changes arrival to 20:31, leaving nine minutes and missing the buffer by one. Call/Response selects at £48 for two and shows 19:43.

A-1440.edge_observation: Tab and Enter restored the usual walk; arrival changed to 19:42 and visible focus remained on Usual walk. Captures: A-1440-before, A-1440-after, A-1440-edge.
A-1440.fact_check: The Call/Response result still says 'Ends 20:16. Walk 15 min' alongside arrival 19:43; an arrival before the stated ending is contradictory. After restoring the walk, that sentence also retains 15 minutes and 19:43. The actual Call/Response end time and arrival cannot be independently confirmed from this view.
A-1440.strength: Three illustrated poses and captions make the reach, shared lean and release legible, while the selection and journey result are easy to compare.
A-1440.weakness: Stale chronological text undermines confidence in the alternate journey.
A-1440.repair: Derive the displayed end time, walk duration and arrival from the selected show and pace together.

primary_action.input: Tab to One minute slower and press Enter; Shift+Tab to Call/Response and press Enter.
primary_action.expected: Recalculate the buffer and alternate journey.
primary_action.observed: Hinge is £60 for two, arriving 20:30 with a 10-minute buffer; joined hands and a mirrored lean indicate shared weight. The slower walk gives 20:31, one minute short of the buffer. Call/Response displays £48 for two and 19:43.

A-390.edge_observation: Keyboard restoration displays 19:42 and leaves visible focus on Usual walk. Captures: A-390-before, A-390-after, A-390-edge.
A-390.fact_check: The result retains 'Ends 20:16. Walk 15 min' and 19:43 after the walk is restored; the stated end also conflicts with either displayed Call/Response arrival. Actual show timing is unsupported by this view.
A-390.strength: At 390 px, three small panels show glossy coral and yellow jointed figures on a blue perspective grid. Their changing poses and captions convey the duet sequence; the art changes for Call/Response.
A-390.weakness: The small figures and narrow captions reduce detail, and the incorrect journey explanation remains prominent.
A-390.repair: Correct the changing chronology and give the choreography more room at mobile widths.

primary_action.observed: Hinge is £60 for two, arriving 20:30 with the assumed 10-minute buffer. Its description identifies joined hands and a mirrored lean as shared-weight movement. The slower walk produces 20:31, missing the buffer by one minute. Call/Response shows £48 for two and 19:43.

B-1440.edge_observation: Keyboard restoration shows 19:42 and keeps visible focus on Usual walk. Captures: B-1440-before, B-1440-after, B-1440-edge.
B-1440.fact_check: The selected Call/Response result combines 19:43 with 'Ends 20:16. Walk 15 min'; after restoration it still says 15 minutes and 19:43 while the main arrival says 19:42. These conflicting facts do not establish the actual alternate journey.
B-1440.strength: Large type, strong selection color and a compact side-by-side result make the task easy to scan.
B-1440.weakness: The three text-only choreography columns remain about Hinge after Call/Response is selected, so the dominant composition no longer describes the chosen show.

primary_action.input: Tab to One minute slower and press Enter; Shift+Tab to Call/Response and press Enter.
primary_action.expected: Show the effect on Hinge’s buffer, then update the show, pair price, arrival and choreography.
primary_action.observed: Hinge changed to 20:31 and missed the 20:30 cutoff by one minute. Call/Response then showed £48 for two and arrival at 19:43.

A-1440.edge_observation: Tab and Enter restored Usual walk (8 min), arrival 19:42, with visible focus remaining on that button.
A-1440.fact_check: Initially Hinge is £60 for two, ends at 20:16 and arrives at 20:30 after a 14-minute walk, exactly meeting the assumed 10-minute buffer for the 20:40 train. Joined palms and a mirrored lean communicate shared weight. The slower 15-minute walk leaves nine minutes. Call/Response ends at 19:34 and arrives at 19:43 with a nine-minute walk. Arithmetic is consistent; actual schedules, fares and walk durations are not independently verified.
A-1440.strength: The three illustrated poses give the reach, shared counterlean and release a physical sequence; the selected middle pose gives the weight transfer emphasis.
A-1440.weakness: The chronology of the shows is only visible one selection at a time, so comparing their end times requires memory.
A-1440.repair: Show each show’s end time alongside its choice while retaining the selected journey calculation.

primary_action.input: Tab to One minute slower and press Enter; Shift+Tab to Call/Response and press Enter.
primary_action.expected: Expose the missed Hinge buffer and update the alternative’s result.
primary_action.observed: Hinge arrived at 20:31, one minute past the cutoff. Call/Response showed £48 for two and 19:43.

A-390.edge_observation: Tab and Enter restored the eight-minute walk and 19:42 arrival; focus remained visibly on Usual walk.
A-390.fact_check: Hinge is initially £60 for two and arrives at 20:30 for the 20:40 train, with an assumed 10-minute buffer. Joined hands and a mirrored lean identify the shared-weight match. The 15-minute walk produces a nine-minute buffer; Call/Response’s nine-minute walk produces 19:43, and its usual eight-minute walk produces 19:42. Displayed arithmetic is consistent; underlying real-world facts are unverified.
A-390.strength: The central panel shows two orange and yellow mannequin-like figures joined at the hands and leaning apart; the smaller flanking poses establish a movement sequence.
A-390.weakness: At 390 px the side figures and captions are small, and the narrow columns force captions into short, fragmented lines. End times still must be compared across selections.
A-390.repair: Give the sequence more legible space on mobile and show both end times in the choices.

B-1440.fact_check: Initially Hinge costs £60 for two and arrives at 20:30, exactly ten minutes before the 20:40 train. Its joined hands and mirrored lean describe shared weight. The slower walk changes arrival to 20:31; Call/Response ends at 19:34 and arrives at 19:43 after nine minutes. Arithmetic is consistent; real schedules, prices and walks are unverified.
B-1440.strength: Large sequential words and short descriptions make the movement phases easy to scan, and the choice and result remain visible together.
B-1440.weakness: The wide choreography area is mostly empty and explains movement only in text; changing shows replaces the end time, making chronology harder to compare.

B-390.edge_observation: Tab and Enter restored the eight-minute walk and 19:42 arrival; focus remained visibly on Usual walk.
B-390.fact_check: Hinge initially costs £60 for two, with arrival at 20:30 and an assumed ten-minute buffer before the 20:40 train. Its joined hands and mirrored lean describe shared weight. At the slower pace Hinge arrives at 20:31; Call/Response arrives at 19:43, or 19:42 after restoring its usual walk. Arithmetic is consistent; the real-world inputs are unverified.
B-390.strength: The compact layout keeps the choices, walk controls and result together, with a clear focus outline.
B-390.weakness: At 390 px the art is three narrow text columns with yellow headings and dividers; there are no dancer images. The words describe the sequence but do not visually convey the shared lean. Show end times disappear when the selection changes.

preference.reason: Both views completed the requested keyboard flow and produced consistent calculations. A’s changing illustrated poses make the difference between shared counterweight and independent response visible as well as verbal, although its mobile side panels need more legibility.
